newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges firm on better demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges firm on better demand.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel oil barges ticked up in early trade on Wednesday on better demand but some players were also said to be trying to push the market up, while cargoes continued to fetch steady to slightly higher prices.
High sulphur barges traded twice at $88.50 fob ARA then $88, compared with Tuesday's highest deal at $87, but then talk moved down to $86.50/$87.50 for buyers and sellers, traders said.
Some were sceptical of the move, saying that a major and a trader were selling at the higher numbers for pricing purposes.
But others said demand has picked up from a day earlier, at some 15,000 tonnes, giving a little push to the market.
"It's like a yo-yo, this market. I don't think there's any real reason for the move upside but I think some people are pricing," one trader said.
Others have said they expected the market to be steady to weakish this week, due to lower overall demand, adding they expected it to pick up next week.
Traders said low sulphur barges were unchanged in the $94/$95 region but a few sellers were at $96.
Russian high sulphur fetched steady to stronger prices.
One trader said that an M-40 out of Klaipeda was sold to a trader.
The 27,000-tonne loader had a price tag of two means +$1.75 for cracked and two means +$6 if it was straight-run, unchanged to a little firmer than Tuesday's levels.
Some traders said that a deal on Tuesday reported done at $95 cif Las Palmas for bunker quality bought by a refiner was actually done on a floating basis.
